source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Identify the appliance model, make, and unique identification number.
3. Record the date and location of the safety check.
4. Document the name of the technician performing the safety check and their qualification status.
5. Capture the specific safety tests performed, including voltage tests, ground continuity, and insulation resistance tests.
6. Describe in detail the failures observed, such as frayed wires, faulty components, or malfunctioning safety switches.
7. Use clear, concise, and complete descriptions for each failure, including exact locations if relevant (such as "fused safety switch on the back left" or "insulation resistance failure at plug").
8. Take photographs where necessary to illustrate failures.
9. Record any calibration status of the testing equipment used.
10. Note any advisories or warnings to users, such as "Do not use until repaired."
11. Make mention of any additional recommended action, such as repair details, disposal advice, or replacement.
12.
